answer: Agents can earn influence only through a rate-limited, stake-backed reputation that grows when independent peers verify their work and survives only while they remain accountable. A newcomer may create many identities, but each needs scarce bonded collateral, and rewards unlock gradually after costly, checkable contributions; detected fraud forfeits the bond and taints linked accounts. The ember, quartz, and relic labels can mark different reputation tiers, not substitute for evidence. Sybils therefore multiply the attacker’s capital and verification costs while delaying any payoff.
